newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk bourse funding to boost secularist education.
newsitem.headline: Turk bourse funding to boost secularist education.

text.p: Istanbul's bourse said it was providing 32 trillion lira ($200 million) to build primary schools in the impoverished southeast of the country to support the government's secularist education plans.

Exchange chairman Tuncay Artun said: "The financing for the project will be met totally from the Istanbul Stock Exchange's own resources and construction will be directed personally by our administration," the statement said.
The right-left coalition under Prime Minister Mesut Yilmaz is seeking to push through secularist plans to increase state education to eight years from five.
Islamists fiercely oppose the move, saying it will undermine the role of religious schools.
Southeast Turkey, ravaged by almost 13 years of armed conflict between the state and Kurdish rebels, has remained less developed than the rest of the country.
